clue.text: Form of those who are at cross-purposes

definitions.text: Form of those who are at cross-purposes

parts.words: Form of those who are at cross-purposes
parts.note: voters mark their choice with a cross, so the form they fill in is used for the purpose of making a cross

explanation.surface: A document for people who keep misunderstanding each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At cross-purposes' usually means talking past each other; here it means people whose purpose is to put a cross on a form, as voters do.
explanation.definitionFit: The slip handed to each voter in an election is marked with an X beside the chosen candidate.

clue.text: What could secure your shirt when you put it on horses

definitions.meaning: a collar fastener at the back of the neck holds a shirt collar in place

definitions.text: when you put it on horses
definitions.meaning: to 'put your shirt on' is to bet everything; betting on a stud of horses is to back them

explanation.surface: A gambler wondering what will hold their shirt on after betting it on a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put your shirt on' is a British idiom for staking everything on a bet; a stud is a group of horses kept for breeding, and to back is to bet on.
explanation.definitionFit: A collar fastener sits at the nape of a shirt; betting on horses from a breeding farm is backing that stable.

clue.text: Fruit taking strain in Ireland

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in Ireland

parts.note: a lime is a green citrus fruit
rick is a sprain or wrench of a joint

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit pulling a muscle while visiting Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' joins the two pieces. RICK (also spelt wrick) is a less common word for a sprained joint. The definition is a little loose: the answer is a city and county in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Shannon is a county town of the Irish Republic.

clue.text: Veto a concoction like an egg

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up, so the letters of the two words before it are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A veto being cooked up like a recipe with eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concoction' is the anagram signal: VETO and A are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-shaped, rounded with one end broader, as botanists describe some leaves.

clue.text: Bit of wine — a very tiny bit indeed

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
an ion is a charged atom or molecule, an extremely small particle

explanation.surface: A small helping of wine, barely a drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' and 'tiny bit' look like the same idea twice; the first is the definition and the second is the particle ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A share or helping of something is a piece of it.

clue.text: Have sheriff's men go on board

parts.note: a posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, the vessel you are on when on board

explanation.surface: A sheriff's deputies boarding a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' only joins the pieces. SS (steamship) stands for being aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To own or hold something is a synonym of having it.

clue.text: Soldiers draw up gin cocktail as well worth the effort

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word draw is read from bottom to top
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: Troops mixing a gin drink and finding it worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns DRAW into WARD and 'cocktail' rearranges GIN into ING. 'As' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satisfying repays the work put in.

clue.text: Mine appears at back-end

indicators.note: 'back' tells you to read the word for end in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tip is the end of something, like a pointed extremity

explanation.surface: A mine shaft appearing at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back-end' reads as one word for the rear; split it, 'back' is the reversal signal for TIP (end).
explanation.definitionFit: A coal mine is also called a colliery shaft or workings.

clue.text: Irishman in a superficial film

parts.note: Pat (Patrick) is a stock name for an Irishman in crosswords
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Irishman acting in a shallow movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie, but here it is a thin layer on a surface. 'In' and 'a' are used as written, not as instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheen or thin coating that forms on old bronze or wood over time.

clue.text: Revolutionary painter

definitions.meaning: something that turns or revolves, such as a lathe operator
J. M. W. ... was an English landscape painter

explanation.definitionFit: A lathe worker spins wood on a lathe; the English Romantic artist J. M. W. shares the surname.

clue.text: Interruption of sentence with point tailing off

definitions.text: Interruption of sentence with point tailing off

parts.words: Interruption of sentence with point tailing off
parts.note: a punctuation mark that breaks up a sentence and looks like a dot with a little tail

explanation.surface: A prison term cut short as its purpose fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' suggests a prison term and 'point' a purpose; really they are grammar and a printed dot with a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark that marks a short pause in a sentence, drawn as a dot with a tail.

clue.text: Started to spray perfume

parts.note: rose means got up or started up, as one rises from a seat
to water plants is to spray them

explanation.surface: Someone beginning to spray scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Started to' reads as one verb phrase; 'to' only joins ROSE and WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant liquid distilled from petals, used as a scent and in cooking.

clue.text: When a tennis player begins to be in prison

definitions.meaning: a point in tennis starts at the moment a player serves
a convict undergoes a term of imprisonment

explanation.surface: A tennis player starting a match and ending up behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment for a tennis player's first stroke of a point; also the phrase for undergoing a jail term.

clue.text: Siren adjusts hair-do

indicators.note: to adjust is to rearrange, so the letters of siren are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman fixing her hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjusts' is the anagram signal for SIREN.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour wash applied to hair at a salon gives it a tint.

clue.text: Relative a Pole finds dirty

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative
N is the abbreviation for north, one of the poles

explanation.surface: A relative finding a Polish person grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a person from Poland; it is the North Pole, N. 'Finds' links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Impure or soiled; the opposite of washed.

clue.text: First person upsetting ringer is hard at first to decorate

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the word for the speaker upside down, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: me is the first person pronoun
a bell is something that rings

indicators.note: 'at first' takes only the opening letter of the word hard

explanation.surface: Someone upsetting a bell-ringer, hard to start with, while decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' turns ME into EM; 'at first' takes H from 'hard'.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn or ornament something with added detail.

clue.text: Leave out leader

definitions.meaning: to omit or pass over something
the captain of a curling or bowls team is called this

explanation.definitionFit: To omit something; also the captain of a curling or bowls rink.

clue.text: Reference to lion Saul mauled about

indicators.note: something mauled about is knocked around and disordered, so the letters of the two names are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mention of the biblical Saul being savaged by a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mauled about' is the anagram signal for LION and SAUL together; 'to' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An indirect mention or hint at something.

clue.text: Fancy ram thought of

parts.note: to fancy or imagine something is to dream it
a tup is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Fancying a ram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective describing the ram but is a verb; 'tup' is British dialect for a male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Invented or conceived, as an idea made up in the mind.

clue.text: Bit of brass returned to border

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the instrument's name is read in reverse

parts.note: a tuba is one instrument of the brass section

explanation.surface: Part of a brass fitting sent back to the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of brass' looks like a fragment of metal, but it is a member of an orchestra's brass section, TUBA, which 'returned' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjoin or touch at the edge; neighbouring plots meet along a boundary.

clue.text: Follow Virginia in labour

indicators.note: 'in' places the state's abbreviation inside the word for follow

parts.note: to trail someone is to follow them
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Tracking someone from Virginia while she is giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In labour' reads as giving birth; 'in' puts VA into TRAIL and 'labour' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Painful toil or hard work; also old usage for childbirth.

clue.text: Petty critic of Ring with leg broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of ring and leg are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A carping critic of an opera cycle whose performer broke a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' is the anagram signal for RING and LEG together; 'of' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who finds fault over trifles.

clue.text: Another agent newsman denied

indicators.note: another version of the word agent is a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A second agent rebuffed by a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' signals a new arrangement of AGENT, giving NEGAT; ED is the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Nullified or contradicted, rendered void.

clue.text: Way to prayerful agreement in part of flower

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
amen is said at the end of a prayer to express assent

explanation.surface: A path leading to a garden where one agrees in prayer among the blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' and 'in' only link the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-bearing male organ of a blossom.

clue.text: Pioneer animatedly producing a mouse

parts.note: an early figure in cartoon animation who created a famous cartoon mouse

explanation.surface: An eager innovator whose invention turns out to be a mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animatedly' looks like 'eagerly' or an anagram signal; it means through animation, the pioneer of cartoon films whose famous creation is Mickey.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt, the American film producer whose studio created Mickey the cartoon rodent.

clue.text: Hearing affliction

definitions.meaning: a court hearing of a case
a hardship or ordeal one must endure

explanation.definitionFit: A court case heard by a judge; also a painful ordeal or test.

clue.text: Tonic made with a sour tang

indicators.note: made here means made up or formed from the letters that follow, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A tonic water mixed with something sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' is the anagram signal for A SOUR TANG; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter aromatic flavouring, the bitters added to pink gin and cocktails.

clue.text: Sentimental agent taking work in

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the word for work goes within the word for agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
OP is the abbreviation for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A soft-hearted agent bringing work home.
explanation.walkthrough: The container signal 'taking ... in' is split around its object, so 'in' is part of the indicator, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish or over-emotional, soft.

clue.text: I'm no good at reforming beggar

parts.note: reforming something is putting it right, mending it
saying you are no good at something is saying 'I can't' do it

explanation.surface: A confession of being hopeless at self-improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reforming' looks like an anagram signal but means repairing: 'I'm no good at reforming' is 'I can't mend', written in the other order.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who lives by asking for alms, such as a friar of a begging order.

clue.text: End of the matter

definitions.meaning: the issue or crux under discussion

explanation.definitionFit: The sharp tip of a pin; also the essential issue in a discussion.

clue.text: No sound of horse

indicators.note: 'sound of' signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a horse's cry is a neigh

explanation.surface: No noise from the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of horse' looks like a description of a neigh; the neigh is heard and spelt as the old word for no.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or parliamentary word for refusal, as in 'ayes and noes'.

clue.text: Leave picture with one break after another

parts.note: a holiday is a break from work
a snap is another kind of break, as a stick snaps

explanation.surface: A photograph of time off with a run of interruptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like a verb but is time off work; the two breaks are a vacation and a fracture.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph taken while on vacation.
